note: Reading the treble clef (note-names:3): the letters tapped up a staff from the G line, then the staff-reading game for the lines, the spaces and the notes on ledger lines, its letter buttons named as they show. The game replaces the old staffs with labels always in view, so the player names a note before seeing its name. The first staff uses the mezzo voice, since the tenor staff is drawn in the treble clef with an 8.

exercise.title: Reading notes in the treble clef
exercise.why: Notes go up the staff line, space, line, space in the order of the letters, so once you know one line by heart you can count to any note from it.

cells.text:
The staff below is in the treble clef, which curls around the second line from the bottom: that line is {{g}}, ringed here. Tap up from the ringed {{g}} and say each letter: the notes go line, space, line, space.
Practice until the letters come in order without looking at the labels.

The game below draws one note on a line of the staff, with "?" under it. Name it by pressing its letter, C to B, under the staff: the game says the note and where it sits, then asks the next one.
Practice until you can name a line without counting up from the G line.

Now the game below asks the notes in the four spaces between the lines. Press the letter of each note as it comes.
If you get one wrong, count up from the bottom space, one letter for each space and line, before you answer the next.

This game asks the notes just under and just above the five lines, some on short lines of their own, the ledger lines. Press the letter of each note as it comes.
If you get lost, count from the nearest line of the staff, one letter for each line or space.
